content.text:
Reproduced it: `snippet(notes_fts, 0, ...)` hardcodes column index `0`, which is the `title` column in `notes_fts`'s column list `["title", "path", "frontmatter_json"]` (and same for `sources_fts`'s `["title", "origin", "author"]`). SQLite's `snippet()` with a fixed column index always pulls from *that* column, regardless of which column the match actually occurred in — so it just echoes the title verbatim instead of showing where the query matched.

The fix is to pass `-1`, which tells FTS5 to pick the best-matching column across the whole row.

content.text:
Bug found and fixed. In `src/wakil/storage/fts.py`, all three FTS5 `snippet()` calls hardcoded column index `0`. For `notes_fts` (columns `title, path, frontmatter_json`) and `sources_fts` (columns `title, origin, author`), column `0` is `title` — so the snippet always echoed the title verbatim regardless of which column the query actually matched. `memories_fts` happened to have `content` at index 0, so it wasn't visibly affected the same way.

Fix: changed the column index from `0` to `-1` in all three queries, which tells FTS5 to pick the best-matching column across the row instead of a hardcoded one. Verified with a throwaway sqlite repro that `-1` correctly surfaces the actual matched column (e.g. `path` when the match is in the filename, not the title).

This also exposed a latent test brittleness: `tests/integration/test_search_cli.py` asserted on `.replace("\n", "")` output, which only worked because the snippet was previously short (duplicate of title) and never wrapped the table. With a real (longer) snippet, Rich's 80-column CliRunner default wrapped the `Ref` column across lines with box-drawing borders in between, breaking the naive string check. Fixed by pinning `COLUMNS=200` in `tests/conftest.py`, matching the existing pattern there of normalizing Rich's output for deterministic tests.

Full suite: 228 passed relevant to this change. The 19 failures in `test_skills_resolver.py`/`test_skills_cli.py` are pre-existing and unrelated — they come from an already-uncommitted, in-progress change to `src/wakil/skills/models.py` (adding a required `description` field to `SkillMetadata`) that predates this session; confirmed via `git stash` that they fail even without my edits.
Next -- even though `qmd_enabled` is `True`, it does not appear to return results for the query `mosaic valuation` -- confirm whether it actually works.

content.text:
Confirmed — QMD search is completely broken right now, independent of the specific query. I set up a real test collection to verify end-to-end (not just read the code):

**Root cause: wrong CLI flags.** `qmd_search()` in `src/wakil/integrations/qmd.py:43` invokes:
```
qmd search "<query>" --format json -n 10 --full-path
```
But the installed `qmd` (v2.1.0) has no `--format` or `--full-path` flags at all — the real flag is a bare `--json` boolean, and `--full` means something unrelated ("output full document instead of snippet"). With the flags `wakil` actually sends, `qmd` silently falls back to its plain-text mode and prints `No results found.` (exit code 0) even when a real match exists. `parse_qmd_results()` then fails to `json.loads()` that text, catches the `JSONDecodeError`, and returns `[]`. Net effect: **every QMD search returns zero hits, for any query**, and it fails silently — no error surfaces anywhere, so `qmd_enabled=True` looks fine while the feature has never worked.

I verified this directly: same query, same indexed doc, only the flags differ:
- `qmd search "mosaic" --format json ...` → `No results found.`
- `qmd search "mosaic" --json` → real JSON hit for the doc

Two more bugs I found while tracing this, once I fed correct JSON through `parse_qmd_results`:
1. **Path mangling** (`_relativize`, qmd.py:90): it strips the `qmd://` prefix then resolves against the *process's* cwd, not the workspace root — so paths come back wrong (e.g. `qmdtest/notes/mosaic-valuation.md` instead of `notes/mosaic-valuation.md`), which would break the FTS dedup and mislead any code using the ref path.
2. **Score dropped for real zero scores** (`_as_float`, qmd.py:98): `item.get("score") or item.get("relevance")` treats a legitimate `0` score as falsy and discards it, yielding `score=None`.

Separately (not a code bug, but relevant): `wakil` never runs `qmd collection add <root>` or indexes the workspace with `qmd`, and `qmd_enabled` is set purely from `shutil.which("qmd")` — so even with the flags fixed, a workspace that was never manually registered as a `qmd` collection will still return zero hits.

# QMD integration: fix broken flags, scope storage per-workspace, add collection management

## Context

`wakil search` shells out to the external `qmd` CLI (a Node/Bun tool) for full-text/hybrid search over the knowledge base. Investigation (via a live reproduction with a real `qmd` install) confirmed `qmd_search()` in `src/wakil/integrations/qmd.py` is **completely non-functional today**: it invokes `qmd <mode> <query> --format json -n <limit> --full-path`, but the installed `qmd` (v2.1.0) has no `--format` or `--full-path` flags at all. Those unrecognized flags cause `qmd` to silently fall back to printing plain text (`No results found.`, exit code 0) instead of JSON — `parse_qmd_results()` then fails to parse that as JSON and returns `[]`. So **every QMD search returns zero hits, for any query**, and it fails completely silently (no error surfaces; `qmd_enabled=True` looks fine while the feature has never worked). The real flag is a bare `--json` boolean; `--full` means something unrelated (full document body vs. snippet).

Two more latent bugs surfaced by feeding real `qmd --json` output through the existing parser:
- `_relativize()` strips the `qmd://` URI prefix but resolves what's left against the **process's cwd**, not the workspace root, so paths come back wrong (e.g. `qmdtest/notes/mosaic-valuation.md` instead of `notes/mosaic-valuation.md`).
- `_as_float(item.get("score") or item.get("relevance"))` treats a legitimate `0` score as falsy, discarding it in favor of `relevance` (usually absent) — silently turning `0.0` into `None`.

Separately, the user wants `qmd`'s own index/collections to stop living in `qmd`'s global, machine-wide default location (`~/.cache/qmd/index.sqlite`, shared across every KB on the machine) and instead be scoped to each wakil workspace, next to `wakil.db`. Investigation of `qmd`'s own source (`@tobilu/qmd` v2.1.0, installed at `~/.bun/install/global/node_modules/@tobilu/qmd`) found it fully supports this via two environment variables it already respects: `INDEX_PATH` (exact override for the index sqlite file path) and `QMD_CONFIG_DIR` (override for where its YAML collections config lives). Literally pointing `INDEX_PATH` at `wakil.db` itself was considered and rejected (per user decision): `qmd` manages its own SQLite schema via an independent Node process with no coordination with wakil's SQLAlchemy connection, which itself has no WAL/locking configured — two independent tools writing the same physical file risks `SQLITE_BUSY` errors. Instead, qmd's index/config will live in a sibling location: `.wakil/qmd/index.sqlite` and `.wakil/qmd/index.yml`, co-located inside the same per-workspace `.wakil/` directory (already `.gitignore`'d wholesale by `WorkspaceConfig.save()`).

Once storage is scoped per-workspace, there's currently no way to register a folder as a `qmd` collection at all — `wakil` never calls `qmd collection add`, so even with the flags fixed, a fresh workspace returns zero results until collections exist. This plan adds `wakil qmd collection add/list/remove`, plus a `wakil qmd sync` command that proposes (with a preview + confirmation, no silent/automatic behavior per this repo's "avoid hidden background behavior" principle) one collection per KB folder that the entity schema already declares a canonical home for (`concepts/`, `people/`, `meetings/`, `sources/`, etc. — from `src/wakil/schema/entities/*.yaml`), intersected with folders that actually exist on disk.

## Scope boundaries (explicitly out of scope)

- No automatic/hidden collection registration wired into `wakil init` or `wakil enrich` — `wakil qmd sync` is an explicit, user-run, previewed command.
- No `qmd embed`/vector-embedding generation — that's a separate, heavy, model-download step; `search` mode (BM25) works immediately after `collection add` without it. Not touched here.
- No `rename`/`--include`/`--exclude` collection toggles — only `add`/`list`/`remove`, matching what's actually asked for.

## Implementation

### 1. `src/wakil/integrations/qmd.py` — fix the broken flags (the reported bug)

In `qmd_search()`: replace `["qmd", mode, query, "--format", "json", "-n", str(limit), "--full-path"]` with `["qmd", mode, query, "--json", "-n", str(limit)]`.

Fix `_as_float`:
```python
def _as_float(value) -> float | None:
    try:
        return float(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
```
and call it as `_as_float(item.get("score")) if item.get("score") is not None else _as_float(item.get("relevance"))` (or equivalent explicit `is not None` chain) instead of `item.get("score") or item.get("relevance")`, so a real `0` score survives.

Fix `_relativize`/`parse_qmd_results` to resolve `qmd://<collection>/<relpath>` correctly:
- Add `_read_collections(qmd_dir: Path) -> dict[str, Path]` that reads `<qmd_dir>/index.yml` (PyYAML, already a dependency) and returns `{name: Path(entry["path"])}` from its `collections:` map; returns `{}` if the file doesn't exist or fails to parse (defensive, matches this module's existing "malformed input yields no results" style).
- `parse_qmd_results(output: str, root: Path, qmd_dir: Path)` (new required `qmd_dir` param) loads that map once and passes it to `_relativize(raw_path, root, collections)`.
- `_relativize`: if `raw_path` starts with `qmd://`, split into `name` + `rel`, look up `collections[name]`, join, resolve, and `.relative_to(root)` (catch `ValueError` and fall back to the stripped `name/rel` string, same defensive spirit as today). Otherwise keep the existing plain-absolute-path handling unchanged (there's an existing test asserting `parse_qmd_results` also accepts bare absolute paths — preserve that).

Add the shared subprocess env helper used by every `qmd` invocation (search and the new collection commands below):
```python
def _qmd_env(qmd_dir: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    return {**os.environ, "QMD_CONFIG_DIR": str(qmd_dir), "INDEX_PATH": str(qmd_dir / "index.sqlite")}
```
`qmd_search()` gains a `qmd_dir: Path` parameter (passed by the caller), uses it for both `_qmd_env` and the `parse_qmd_results` call.

Fix `detect_qmd`'s dead/inaccurate `project_index` check (currently checks `(root / ".qmd").exists()`, which doesn't correspond to anything real `qmd` does — confirmed by reading `qmd`'s source, and confirmed this field is currently computed and unit-tested but never actually displayed anywhere in `ui/console.py`). Change it to accept a `qmd_dir: Path | None` and check `(qmd_dir / "index.sqlite").exists()` instead — this makes it a real, meaningful signal ("has this workspace been given a qmd index yet") that Step 4 below will finally surface in `print_status`.

### 2. `src/wakil/config/settings.py` — new per-workspace qmd storage path

Add `QMD_DIRNAME = "qmd"` alongside the existing `WAKIL_DIR`/`CONFIG_FILENAME`/`DATABASE_FILENAME` constants, and a `WorkspaceConfig.qmd_dir` property: `self.wakil_dir / QMD_DIRNAME` (same pattern as the existing `database_path`/`config_path` properties). This becomes the one place the `.wakil/qmd/` convention is defined; every other call site imports/derives from here rather than re-deriving the path.

### 3. Wire the new storage path through existing call sites

- `src/wakil/app/search_service.py:43` — `qmd_search(config.root_path, query, limit=limit, mode=mode)` → `qmd_search(config.root_path, config.qmd_dir, query, limit=limit, mode=mode)`.
- `src/wakil/app/workspace_service.py` — both call sites of `detect_qmd(root)` (in `init_workspace` and `get_status`) pass `qmd_dir=root / WAKIL_DIR / QMD_DIRNAME` (import those two constants; config may not exist yet at the `init_workspace` call site, so this is computed directly rather than via `config.qmd_dir`).

### 4. Surface the (previously dead) project-index signal in status output

`src/wakil/ui/console.py::print_status` — add a row showing whether the workspace has its own qmd index yet (using the now-meaningful `status.qmd.project_index`), e.g. `"QMD index"` → `"[green]workspace-scoped[/green]"` vs `"[dim]not yet created (run 'wakil qmd sync')[/dim]"`. Small, self-evidently useful now that the field means something real.

### 5. New collection-management functions — `src/wakil/integrations/qmd.py`

```python
@dataclass
class QmdCollection:
    name: str
    path: Path
    pattern: str

@dataclass
class QmdCommandResult:
    success: bool
    message: str
```
- `qmd_list_collections(qmd_dir: Path) -> list[QmdCollection]` — reads `_read_collections` directly (no subprocess needed; `qmd collection list` has no JSON output mode, so reading the YAML config we already own is more robust than screen-scraping colored text).
- `qmd_add_collection(root: Path, qmd_dir: Path, path: Path, name: str | None, pattern: str | None) -> QmdCommandResult` — runs `qmd collection add <abs-path> [--mask <pattern>] [--name <name>]` with `_qmd_env(qmd_dir)`, `cwd=root`; captures stdout/stderr and returns a structured success/message result (unlike `qmd_search`, this is a user-triggered mutating command, so failures — "binary missing", non-zero exit, timeout — must be reported, not silently swallowed).
- `qmd_remove_collection(qmd_dir: Path, name: str) -> QmdCommandResult` — runs `qmd collection remove <name>` with the same env.

### 6. `src/wakil/app/qmd_service.py` (new file) — path validation + the auto-generation strategy

- `add_collection(config: WorkspaceConfig, path: Path, name: str | None, pattern: str | None) -> QmdCommandResult` — resolves `path` (relative → relative to `config.root_path`), rejects it if it escapes `config.root_path` (mirrors the existing path-escape defense in `skills/resolver.py`), then delegates to `qmd.qmd_add_collection`.
- `plan_default_collections(config: WorkspaceConfig) -> list[CollectionPlan]` — the auto-generation strategy: union of every `directory` value from `load_entity_schemas()` (`src/wakil/schema/loader.py`) plus `config.ingest_directory` and `config.generated_directory`, filtered to directories that actually exist under `config.root_path`, filtered again against `qmd.qmd_list_collections(config.qmd_dir)` to skip already-registered ones. Collection name = the relative dir with `/` replaced by `-` (e.g. `ideas/reflections` → `ideas-reflections`); pattern = `**/*.md`.
```python
@dataclass
class CollectionPlan:
    name: str
    path: str      # relative to workspace root
    pattern: str
```

### 7. CLI — `src/wakil/cli/main.py`

New two-level Typer nesting (a new structural pattern for this file — every existing sub-app like `schema_app`/`skills_app` is one level deep, so call this out explicitly in the PR description):
```python
qmd_app = typer.Typer(help="Manage the QMD search index and collections.", no_args_is_help=True)
app.add_typer(qmd_app, name="qmd")
qmd_collection_app = typer.Typer(help="Manage QMD collections (indexed folders).", no_args_is_help=True)
qmd_app.add_typer(qmd_collection_app, name="collection")
```
Commands, following the `memory_app`/`schema_app` convention (lazy imports inside the command body, service call, then a `print_*` helper):
- `qmd_collection_app.command("add")` — args: `path: Path`, `--name`, `--pattern`; calls `qmd_service.add_collection`, prints success/failure.
- `qmd_collection_app.command("list")` — calls `qmd.qmd_list_collections`, prints via new `print_qmd_collections`.
- `qmd_collection_app.command("remove")` — arg: `name: str`; calls `qmd.qmd_remove_collection`.
- `qmd_app.command("sync")` — calls `qmd_service.plan_default_collections`, prints a preview table (new `print_qmd_collection_plan`, modeled on `print_migration_plan`'s preview-before-apply shape), prompts for confirmation unless `--yes`/`-y`, then calls `qmd_service.add_collection` for each planned entry and reports results.

### 8. `src/wakil/ui/console.py` — new print helpers

`print_qmd_collections(collections: list[QmdCollection])` and `print_qmd_collection_plan(plans: list[CollectionPlan])`, both plain `rich.Table`s following the exact shape of `print_search_hits`/existing tables in this file.

## Tests

- `tests/unit/test_qmd.py` (existing file, needs real edits, not just additions):
  - `test_qmd_search_invokes_expected_command` currently asserts the *buggy* command (`--format json ... --full-path`) — rewrite to assert `--json` and no `--full-path`, and that `env` includes `QMD_CONFIG_DIR`/`INDEX_PATH` pointing at the passed `qmd_dir`.
  - `test_detect_reports_project_index` currently creates `(tmp_path / ".qmd")` — rewrite to create `<qmd_dir>/index.sqlite` and pass `qmd_dir` into `detect_qmd`.
  - Add: zero-score survives `_as_float`; `qmd://` URI resolves correctly via a fake `index.yml` fixture; `qmd_add_collection`/`qmd_list_collections`/`qmd_remove_collection` via monkeypatched `subprocess.run` (same pattern as the existing `fake_run` fixture in this file).
- New `tests/unit/test_qmd_service.py`: `plan_default_collections` against a fixture-like tmp KB with a few schema-directory folders present/absent, and one pre-existing registered collection to prove it's skipped; `add_collection` path-escape rejection.
- New `tests/integration/test_qmd_cli.py`: `wakil qmd collection add/list/remove` and `wakil qmd sync` through `CliRunner`, with `subprocess.run`/`shutil.which` monkeypatched (CI likely doesn't have the real `qmd` binary — same constraint the existing unit tests already work around).

## Verification

1. `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_qmd.py tests/unit/test_qmd_service.py tests/integration/test_qmd_cli.py -q` — all green.
2. `uv run pytest -q` (full suite) — no regressions (already have a baseline of 19 known-unrelated pre-existing failures from in-progress `skills/models.py` work on this branch; confirm no *new* failures beyond that baseline).
3. Manual end-to-end, since `qmd` is genuinely installed on this machine:
   - Build a scratch KB with a `concepts/` folder containing a note.
   - `wakil init <scratch-kb>`
   - `wakil qmd sync` → confirm the preview lists `concepts` (and any other existing schema dirs), confirm registration.
   - Inspect `<scratch-kb>/.wakil/qmd/` — confirm `index.sqlite` and `index.yml` now exist there (not under `~/.cache/qmd/`).
   - `wakil search "<term from the note>"` → confirm a real QMD hit comes back with a correct `ref` path and non-null score (this is the original reported bug — must actually return results now).
   - `wakil qmd collection list` / `wakil qmd collection remove <name>` → confirm both work and reflect in `.wakil/qmd/index.yml`.

## Approved Plan:
# QMD integration: fix broken flags, scope storage per-workspace, add collection management

## Context

`wakil search` shells out to the external `qmd` CLI (a Node/Bun tool) for full-text/hybrid search over the knowledge base. Investigation (via a live reproduction with a real `qmd` install) confirmed `qmd_search()` in `src/wakil/integrations/qmd.py` is **completely non-functional today**: it invokes `qmd <mode> <query> --format json -n <limit> --full-path`, but the installed `qmd` (v2.1.0) has no `--format` or `--full-path` flags at all. Those unrecognized flags cause `qmd` to silently fall back to printing plain text (`No results found.`, exit code 0) instead of JSON — `parse_qmd_results()` then fails to parse that as JSON and returns `[]`. So **every QMD search returns zero hits, for any query**, and it fails completely silently (no error surfaces; `qmd_enabled=True` looks fine while the feature has never worked). The real flag is a bare `--json` boolean; `--full` means something unrelated (full document body vs. snippet).

Two more latent bugs surfaced by feeding real `qmd --json` output through the existing parser:
- `_relativize()` strips the `qmd://` URI prefix but resolves what's left against the **process's cwd**, not the workspace root, so paths come back wrong (e.g. `qmdtest/notes/mosaic-valuation.md` instead of `notes/mosaic-valuation.md`).
- `_as_float(item.get("score") or item.get("relevance"))` treats a legitimate `0` score as falsy, discarding it in favor of `relevance` (usually absent) — silently turning `0.0` into `None`.

Separately, the user wants `qmd`'s own index/collections to stop living in `qmd`'s global, machine-wide default location (`~/.cache/qmd/index.sqlite`, shared across every KB on the machine) and instead be scoped to each wakil workspace, next to `wakil.db`. Investigation of `qmd`'s own source (`@tobilu/qmd` v2.1.0, installed at `~/.bun/install/global/node_modules/@tobilu/qmd`) found it fully supports this via two environment variables it already respects: `INDEX_PATH` (exact override for the index sqlite file path) and `QMD_CONFIG_DIR` (override for where its YAML collections config lives). Literally pointing `INDEX_PATH` at `wakil.db` itself was considered and rejected (per user decision): `qmd` manages its own SQLite schema via an independent Node process with no coordination with wakil's SQLAlchemy connection, which itself has no WAL/locking configured — two independent tools writing the same physical file risks `SQLITE_BUSY` errors. Instead, qmd's index/config will live in a sibling location: `.wakil/qmd/index.sqlite` and `.wakil/qmd/index.yml`, co-located inside the same per-workspace `.wakil/` directory (already `.gitignore`'d wholesale by `WorkspaceConfig.save()`).

Once storage is scoped per-workspace, there's currently no way to register a folder as a `qmd` collection at all — `wakil` never calls `qmd collection add`, so even with the flags fixed, a fresh workspace returns zero results until collections exist. This plan adds `wakil qmd collection add/list/remove`, plus a `wakil qmd sync` command that proposes (with a preview + confirmation, no silent/automatic behavior per this repo's "avoid hidden background behavior" principle) one collection per KB folder that the entity schema already declares a canonical home for (`concepts/`, `people/`, `meetings/`, `sources/`, etc. — from `src/wakil/schema/entities/*.yaml`), intersected with folders that actually exist on disk.

## Scope boundaries (explicitly out of scope)

- No automatic/hidden collection registration wired into `wakil init` or `wakil enrich` — `wakil qmd sync` is an explicit, user-run, previewed command.
- No `qmd embed`/vector-embedding generation — that's a separate, heavy, model-download step; `search` mode (BM25) works immediately after `collection add` without it. Not touched here.
- No `rename`/`--include`/`--exclude` collection toggles — only `add`/`list`/`remove`, matching what's actually asked for.

### 1. `src/wakil/integrations/qmd.py` — fix the broken flags (the reported bug)

In `qmd_search()`: replace `["qmd", mode, query, "--format", "json", "-n", str(limit), "--full-path"]` with `["qmd", mode, query, "--json", "-n", str(limit)]`.

Fix `_as_float`:
```python
def _as_float(value) -> float | None:
    try:
        return float(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
```
and call it as `_as_float(item.get("score")) if item.get("score") is not None else _as_float(item.get("relevance"))` (or equivalent explicit `is not None` chain) instead of `item.get("score") or item.get("relevance")`, so a real `0` score survives.

Fix `_relativize`/`parse_qmd_results` to resolve `qmd://<collection>/<relpath>` correctly:
- Add `_read_collections(qmd_dir: Path) -> dict[str, Path]` that reads `<qmd_dir>/index.yml` (PyYAML, already a dependency) and returns `{name: Path(entry["path"])}` from its `collections:` map; returns `{}` if the file doesn't exist or fails to parse (defensive, matches this module's existing "malformed input yields no results" style).
- `parse_qmd_results(output: str, root: Path, qmd_dir: Path)` (new required `qmd_dir` param) loads that map once and passes it to `_relativize(raw_path, root, collections)`.
- `_relativize`: if `raw_path` starts with `qmd://`, split into `name` + `rel`, look up `collections[name]`, join, resolve, and `.relative_to(root)` (catch `ValueError` and fall back to the stripped `name/rel` string, same defensive spirit as today). Otherwise keep the existing plain-absolute-path handling unchanged (there's an existing test asserting `parse_qmd_results` also accepts bare absolute paths — preserve that).

    return {**os.environ, "QMD_CONFIG_DIR": str(qmd_dir), "INDEX_PATH": str(qmd_dir / "index.sqlite")}

5	remain the source of truth; `.wakil/` is operational state only.
6	"""

9	
10	from pathlib import Path
11	
12	import yaml
13	from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

16	CONFIG_FILENAME = "config.yaml"
17	DATABASE_FILENAME = "wakil.db"
18

20	SPECIAL_FILES = ("README.md", "AGENTS.md", "SCHEMA.md", "RESOLVER.md")
21

23	class WorkspaceConfig(BaseModel):
24	    """Persisted per-workspace settings."""
25	
26	    name: str
27	    root_path: Path
28	    git_remote: str | None = None
29	    qmd_enabled: bool = False
30	    ingest_directory: str = Field(default="sources")
31	    generated_directory: str = Field(default="drafts")
32

35	        return self.root_path / WAKIL_DIR
36

39	        return self.wakil_dir / DATABASE_FILENAME
40	
41	    @property
42	    def config_path(self) -> Path:
43	        return self.wakil_dir / CONFIG_FILENAME
44

46	        self.wakil_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
47	        # Operational state stays out of the knowledge base's git history.
48	        gitignore = self.wakil_dir / ".gitignore"
49	        if not gitignore.exists():
50	            gitignore.write_text("*\n", encoding="utf-8")
51	        data = self.model_dump(mode="json")
52	        self.config_path.write_text(yaml.safe_dump(data, sort_keys=False), encoding="utf-8")
53

56	        config_path = root / WAKIL_DIR / CONFIG_FILENAME
57	        data = yaml.safe_load(config_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
58	        # The workspace may have been moved or checked out elsewhere; trust
59	        # the directory the config was found in over the stored path.

1	"""QMD integration: detection and search.
2	
3	QMD (https://github.com/tobi/qmd) is the first-class search engine for the
4	knowledge base. It offers three modes: `search` (BM25 keyword), `vsearch`
5	(vector similarity), and `query` (hybrid with LLM re-ranking). Results are
6	requested as JSON with filesystem paths so they map back to notes.
7	"""
8	
9	import json
10	import shutil
11	import subprocess
12	from dataclasses import dataclass
13	from pathlib import Path
14	
15	SEARCH_MODES = ("search", "vsearch", "query")
16	
17	
18	@dataclass
19	class QmdInfo:
20	    available: bool
21	    version: str | None = None
22	    workspace_scripts: list[str] | None = None
23	    project_index: bool = False
24	
25	
26	@dataclass
27	class QmdResult:
28	    path: str
29	    score: float | None = None
30	    snippet: str = ""
31	    title: str | None = None
32	    docid: str | None = None
33	
34	
35	def qmd_search(root: Path, query: str, limit: int = 10, mode: str = "search") -> list[QmdResult]:
36	    """Run a QMD search from the workspace root; empty list if unavailable."""
37	    if mode not in SEARCH_MODES:
38	        raise ValueError(f"unknown qmd mode: {mode}")
39	    if shutil.which("qmd") is None:
40	        return []
41	    try:
42	        result = subprocess.run(
43	            ["qmd", mode, query, "--format", "json", "-n", str(limit), "--full-path"],
44	            capture_output=True,
45	            text=True,
46	            timeout=120,
47	            cwd=root,
48	        )
49	    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
50	        return []
51	    if result.returncode != 0:
52	        return []
53	    return parse_qmd_results(result.stdout, root)
54	
55	
56	def parse_qmd_results(output: str, root: Path) -> list[QmdResult]:
57	    """Parse QMD JSON output defensively; malformed output yields no results."""
58	    try:
59	        data = json.loads(output)
60	    except json.JSONDecodeError:
61	        return []
62	    if isinstance(data, dict):
63	        items = data.get("results") or data.get("documents") or []
64	    elif isinstance(data, list):
65	        items = data
66	    else:
67	        return []
68	
69	    results = []
70	    for item in items:
71	        if not isinstance(item, dict):
72	            continue
73	        raw_path = item.get("file") or item.get("path") or item.get("filepath") or ""
74	        if not raw_path:
75	            continue
76	        results.append(
77	            QmdResult(
78	                path=_relativize(str(raw_path), root),
79	                score=_as_float(item.get("score") or item.get("relevance")),
80	                snippet=str(
81	                    item.get("snippet") or item.get("excerpt") or item.get("context") or ""
82	                ),
83	                title=item.get("title"),
84	                docid=item.get("docid") or item.get("id"),
85	            )
86	        )
87	    return results
88	
89	
90	def _relativize(raw_path: str, root: Path) -> str:
91	    path = raw_path.removeprefix("qmd://")
92	    try:
93	        return str(Path(path).resolve().relative_to(root.resolve()))
94	    except ValueError:
95	        return path
96	
97	
98	def _as_float(value) -> float | None:
99	    try:
100	        return float(value)
101	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
102	        return None
103	
104	
105	def detect_qmd(root: Path | None = None) -> QmdInfo:
106	    binary = shutil.which("qmd")
107	    version: str | None = None
108	    if binary:
109	        try:
110	            result = subprocess.run(
111	                [binary, "--version"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10
112	            )
113	            if result.returncode == 0:
114	                version = result.stdout.strip() or None
115	        except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
116	            pass
117	
118	    scripts: list[str] | None = None
119	    project_index = False
120	    if root is not None:
121	        bin_dir = root / "bin"
122	        if bin_dir.is_dir():
123	            found = sorted(p.name for p in bin_dir.glob("qmd-*"))
124	            scripts = found or None
125	        project_index = (root / ".qmd").exists()
126	
127	    return QmdInfo(
128	        available=binary is not None,
129	        version=version,
130	        workspace_scripts=scripts,
131	        project_index=project_index,
132	    )

"""QMD collection management: path validation and the default-collection strategy."""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from wakil.config.settings import WorkspaceConfig
from wakil.integrations import qmd
from wakil.integrations.qmd import QmdCommandResult
from wakil.schema.loader import load_entity_schemas


@dataclass
class CollectionPlan:
    name: str
    path: str  # relative to workspace root
    pattern: str


class QmdPathError(Exception):
    """A collection path escapes the workspace root."""


def add_collection(
    config: WorkspaceConfig, path: Path, name: str | None = None, pattern: str | None = None
) -> QmdCommandResult:
    """Register `path` (relative to the workspace root, or already inside it)
    as a qmd collection. Rejects paths that resolve outside the workspace."""
    root = config.root_path.resolve()
    candidate = path if path.is_absolute() else root / path
    candidate = candidate.resolve()
    try:
        candidate.relative_to(root)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise QmdPathError(f"{path} resolves outside the workspace root {root}.") from exc

    config.qmd_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return qmd.qmd_add_collection(root, config.qmd_dir, candidate, name=name, pattern=pattern)


def plan_default_collections(config: WorkspaceConfig) -> list[CollectionPlan]:
    """Propose one collection per KB folder that the entity schema declares a
    canonical home for (concepts/, people/, meetings/, sources/, ...),
    intersected with folders that actually exist and aren't already registered.
    """
    schemas = load_entity_schemas()
    candidate_dirs = {schema.directory for schema in schemas.values() if schema.directory}
    candidate_dirs.add(config.ingest_directory)
    candidate_dirs.add(config.generated_directory)

    existing_names = {c.name for c in qmd.qmd_list_collections(config.qmd_dir)}

    plans = []
    for rel_dir in sorted(candidate_dirs):
        if not (config.root_path / rel_dir).is_dir():
            continue
        name = rel_dir.replace("/", "-")
        if name in existing_names:
            continue
        plans.append(CollectionPlan(name=name, path=rel_dir, pattern=qmd.DEFAULT_PATTERN))
    return plans

import json
from pathlib import Path

from wakil.integrations import qmd


def test_parse_results_list_shape(tmp_path: Path):
    qmd_dir = tmp_path / ".wakil" / "qmd"
    output = json.dumps(
        [
            {
                "file": str(tmp_path / "concepts" / "graph-memory.md"),
                "score": 0.92,
                "snippet": "graph memory ...",
                "title": "Graph Memory",
                "docid": "#abc123",
            }
        ]
    )
    results = qmd.parse_qmd_results(output, tmp_path, qmd_dir)
    assert len(results) == 1
    assert results[0].path == "concepts/graph-memory.md"
    assert results[0].score == 0.92
    assert results[0].docid == "#abc123"


def test_parse_results_dict_shape_and_qmd_uri_without_registry(tmp_path: Path):
    """With no index.yml (collection unknown), a qmd:// URI falls back to the
    stripped name/relpath string rather than crashing."""
    qmd_dir = tmp_path / ".wakil" / "qmd"
    output = json.dumps({"results": [{"path": "qmd://notes/a.md", "relevance": "0.5"}]})
    results = qmd.parse_qmd_results(output, tmp_path, qmd_dir)
    assert len(results) == 1
    assert results[0].path == "notes/a.md"
    assert results[0].score == 0.5


def test_parse_results_resolves_qmd_uri_via_collection_registry(tmp_path: Path):
    qmd_dir = tmp_path / ".wakil" / "qmd"
    qmd_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
    (tmp_path / "concepts").mkdir()
    (qmd_dir / "index.yml").write_text(
        "collections:\n"
        "  concepts:\n"
        f"    path: {tmp_path / 'concepts'}\n"
        "    pattern: '**/*.md'\n"
    )
    output = json.dumps([{"file": "qmd://concepts/graph-memory.md", "score": 0.5}])
    results = qmd.parse_qmd_results(output, tmp_path, qmd_dir)
    assert results[0].path == "concepts/graph-memory.md"


def test_parse_results_zero_score_survives(tmp_path: Path):
    qmd_dir = tmp_path / ".wakil" / "qmd"
    output = json.dumps([{"file": str(tmp_path / "a.md"), "score": 0}])
    results = qmd.parse_qmd_results(output, tmp_path, qmd_dir)
    assert results[0].score == 0.0


def test_parse_results_tolerates_garbage(tmp_path: Path):
    qmd_dir = tmp_path / ".wakil" / "qmd"
    assert qmd.parse_qmd_results("not json", tmp_path, qmd_dir) == []
    assert qmd.parse_qmd_results("42", tmp_path, qmd_dir) == []
    assert qmd.parse_qmd_results(json.dumps([{"no_path": True}, "junk"]), tmp_path, qmd_dir) == []


def test_qmd_search_returns_empty_when_binary_missing(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(qmd.shutil, "which", lambda _: None)
    assert qmd.qmd_search(tmp_path, tmp_path / ".wakil" / "qmd", "anything") == []


def test_qmd_search_invokes_expected_command(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch):
    captured = {}
    qmd_dir = tmp_path / ".wakil" / "qmd"

    class FakeCompleted:
        returncode = 0
        stdout = json.dumps([{"file": str(tmp_path / "a.md"), "score": 1.0}])

    def fake_run(cmd, **kwargs):
        captured["cmd"] = cmd
        captured["cwd"] = kwargs.get("cwd")
        captured["env"] = kwargs.get("env")
        return FakeCompleted()

    monkeypatch.setattr(qmd.shutil, "which", lambda _: "/usr/bin/qmd")
    monkeypatch.setattr(qmd.subprocess, "run", fake_run)

    results = qmd.qmd_search(tmp_path, qmd_dir, "claims routing", limit=5, mode="vsearch")
    assert captured["cmd"] == ["qmd", "vsearch", "claims routing", "--json", "-n", "5"]
    assert captured["cwd"] == tmp_path
    assert captured["env"]["QMD_CONFIG_DIR"] == str(qmd_dir)

from pathlib import Path

import yaml
from typer.testing import CliRunner

from wakil.cli.main import app

runner = CliRunner()


def _fake_qmd_run(qmd_dir: Path):
    """A stand-in for the real qmd binary: only implements `collection add`
    and `collection remove` against the YAML config file, mirroring the real
    tool's own behavior closely enough to exercise the round trip."""

    class FakeCompleted:
        def __init__(self, returncode=0, stdout="", stderr=""):
            self.returncode = returncode
            self.stdout = stdout
            self.stderr = stderr

    def fake_run(cmd, **kwargs):
        config_path = qmd_dir / "index.yml"
        data = {}
        if config_path.is_file():
            data = yaml.safe_load(config_path.read_text()) or {}
        data.setdefault("collections", {})

        if cmd[:3] == ["qmd", "collection", "add"]:
            path = cmd[3]
            name = None
            pattern = "**/*.md"
            i = 4
            while i < len(cmd):
                if cmd[i] == "--name":
                    name = cmd[i + 1]
                    i += 2
                elif cmd[i] == "--mask":
                    pattern = cmd[i + 1]
                    i += 2
                else:
                    i += 1
            name = name or Path(path).name
            if name in data["collections"]:
                return FakeCompleted(returncode=1, stderr=f"Collection '{name}' already exists.\n")
            data["collections"][name] = {"path": path, "pattern": pattern}
            qmd_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            config_path.write_text(yaml.safe_dump(data))
            return FakeCompleted(stdout=f"Collection '{name}' created successfully\n")

        if cmd[:3] == ["qmd", "collection", "remove"]:
            name = cmd[3]
            if name not in data["collections"]:
                return FakeCompleted(returncode=1, stderr=f"Collection not found: {name}\n")
            del data["collections"][name]
            config_path.write_text(yaml.safe_dump(data))
            return FakeCompleted(stdout=f"Removed collection '{name}'\n")

        return FakeCompleted(returncode=1, stderr="unsupported in test double")

    return fake_run


def _patch_qmd(monkeypatch, qmd_dir: Path):
    monkeypatch.setattr("wakil.integrations.qmd.shutil.which", lambda name: "/usr/bin/qmd")
    monkeypatch.setattr("wakil.integrations.qmd.subprocess.run", _fake_qmd_run(qmd_dir))


def test_qmd_collection_add_then_list(kb_path: Path, monkeypatch):
    runner.invoke(app, ["init", str(kb_path)])
    qmd_dir = kb_path / ".wakil" / "qmd"
    _patch_qmd(monkeypatch, qmd_dir)

    result = runner.invoke(app, ["-w", str(kb_path), "qmd", "collection", "add", "concepts"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output

    result = runner.invoke(app, ["-w", str(kb_path), "qmd", "collection", "list"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0
    assert "concepts" in result.output.replace("\n", "")


def test_qmd_collection_add_rejects_escaping_path(kb_path: Path, monkeypatch):
    runner.invoke(app, ["init", str(kb_path)])
    qmd_dir = kb_path / ".wakil" / "qmd"
    _patch_qmd(monkeypatch, qmd_dir)

    result = runner.invoke(app, ["-w", str(kb_path), "qmd", "collection", "add", "../outside"])
    assert result.exit_code == 1


def test_qmd_collection_remove(kb_path: Path, monkeypatch):
    runner.invoke(app, ["init", str(kb_path)])
    qmd_dir = kb_path / ".wakil" / "qmd"
    _patch_qmd(monkeypatch, qmd_dir)

    runner.invoke(app, ["-w", str(kb_path), "qmd", "collection", "add", "concepts"])
    result = runner.invoke(app, ["-w", str(kb_path), "qmd", "collection", "remove", "concepts"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output

    result = runner.invoke(app, ["-w", str(kb_path), "qmd", "collection", "list"])
    assert "No QMD collections registered" in result.output


def test_qmd_sync_preview_and_confirm(kb_path: Path, monkeypatch):
    runner.invoke(app, ["init", str(kb_path)])
    qmd_dir = kb_path / ".wakil" / "qmd"
    _patch_qmd(monkeypatch, qmd_dir)

    result = runner.invoke(app, ["-w", str(kb_path), "qmd", "sync"], input="y\n")
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    assert "concepts" in result.output.replace("\n", "")

    result = runner.invoke(app, ["-w", str(kb_path), "qmd", "collection", "list"])
    assert "concepts" in result.output.replace("\n", "")


def test_qmd_sync_declines_without_confirmation(kb_path: Path, monkeypatch):
    runner.invoke(app, ["init", str(kb_path)])
    qmd_dir = kb_path / ".wakil" / "qmd"
    _patch_qmd(monkeypatch, qmd_dir)

    result = runner.invoke(app, ["-w", str(kb_path), "qmd", "sync"], input="n\n")
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output

    result = runner.invoke(app, ["-w", str(kb_path), "qmd", "collection", "list"])
    assert "No QMD collections registered" in result.output


def test_qmd_sync_yes_flag_skips_prompt(kb_path: Path, monkeypatch):
    runner.invoke(app, ["init", str(kb_path)])
    qmd_dir = kb_path / ".wakil" / "qmd"
    _patch_qmd(monkeypatch, qmd_dir)

    result = runner.invoke(app, ["-w", str(kb_path), "qmd", "sync", "--yes"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output

    result = runner.invoke(app, ["-w", str(kb_path), "qmd", "collection", "list"])
    assert "concepts" in result.output.replace("\n", "")

Everything's implemented and verified end-to-end with the real `qmd` binary. Summary:

**Fixed the reported bug**: `qmd_search()` was invoking nonexistent flags (`--format json`, `--full-path`), causing `qmd` to silently fall back to plain-text `"No results found."` — every QMD search returned zero hits, always. Now uses the real `--json` flag; verified live that `wakil search "mosaic valuation"` returns an actual hit with `Via=qmd`.

**Storage relocated per-workspace**: QMD's index (`index.sqlite`) and collections config (`index.yml`) now live at `.wakil/qmd/` next to `wakil.db`, via the `INDEX_PATH`/`QMD_CONFIG_DIR` env vars qmd already respects — not the global `~/.cache/qmd/`. Kept as a sibling file rather than merged into `wakil.db` itself (your call, after flagging the lock-contention risk of two uncoordinated tools sharing one SQLite file).

**New commands**:
- `wakil qmd collection add/list/remove` — manual collection management, with path-escape protection.
- `wakil qmd sync` — proposes one collection per KB folder the entity schema already declares a home for (`concepts/`, `people/`, `meetings/`, `sources/`, etc., intersected with what actually exists on disk), previews before registering, and requires confirmation (or `--yes`) — no silent/automatic behavior.
- `wakil status` now shows whether the workspace has its own QMD index yet (a field that existed but was previously dead/unused).

Also fixed two latent bugs found while wiring this up: a falsy-zero bug that dropped real `0` relevance scores, and incorrect path resolution for `qmd://` result URIs (now resolved via the collection registry instead of the process's cwd).

**Tests**: 21 new/updated tests across `test_qmd.py`, new `test_qmd_service.py`, and new `test_qmd_cli.py` — all passing. Full suite: 249 passed, same pre-existing 19 unrelated failures as before (from in-progress `skills/models.py` work on this branch, confirmed via `git stash` earlier).

content.text:
Single collection is very likely the better default, and the reason comes straight from `qmd`'s own engine, not from operational overhead:

**BM25 scoring is computed over one shared FTS5 index (`documents_fts`) for the whole db** — collections are just a filter tag applied *after* scoring, not separate indexes with their own corpus statistics (I confirmed this in `qmd`'s source: the query builds a CTE over the full FTS5 table, ranks it, then optionally filters by collection). So splitting by entity type buys you **zero** ranking-quality improvement — a "meetings" collection and a monolithic KB collection score matches identically.

What splitting *does* buy you: the ability to scope a query (`-c meetings`) or exclude a folder from default results (`includeByDefault: false` — e.g. keeping `sensitive/` out of everyday search). If you don't need either of those, one collection over the whole KB is simpler and avoids maintenance (re-registering as new folders appear).

One concrete bug this raises in what I just built: `qmd` keys documents by `(collection, path)`, and `plan_default_collections` currently proposes both `ideas` and `ideas/reflections` as separate collections (since both are in the entity-schema directory map) — since `ideas`'s glob already covers `ideas/reflections/`, those files would get indexed and embedded **twice**, showing up as duplicate search hits. Want me to fix that (skip a directory if it's nested inside another already-planned one), or would you rather simplify `qmd sync` to just propose one whole-KB collection by default and drop the per-type strategy entirely?
create a single collection by default when running `wakil init` (with a flag to skip).  And, `wakil qmd sync` should propose creating a single collection when none exist.

"""QMD collection management: path validation and the default-collection strategy.

QMD's BM25 scoring runs over one shared FTS5 index regardless of collection
boundaries — collections are a filter applied after scoring, not separate
indexes with separate corpus statistics. Splitting the KB into many
per-folder/per-type collections therefore buys nothing for ranking quality,
and risks double-indexing files that fall under two overlapping directories.
The default strategy here is a single collection covering the whole
workspace; users who want to filter or exclude a folder can still add/remove
collections by hand via `wakil qmd collection add/remove`.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from wakil.config.settings import WorkspaceConfig
from wakil.integrations import qmd
from wakil.integrations.qmd import QmdCommandResult


@dataclass
class CollectionPlan:
    name: str
    path: str  # relative to workspace root
    pattern: str


class QmdPathError(Exception):
    """A collection path escapes the workspace root."""


def add_collection(
    config: WorkspaceConfig, path: Path, name: str | None = None, pattern: str | None = None
) -> QmdCommandResult:
    """Register `path` (relative to the workspace root, or already inside it)
    as a qmd collection. Rejects paths that resolve outside the workspace."""
    root = config.root_path.resolve()
    candidate = path if path.is_absolute() else root / path
    candidate = candidate.resolve()
    try:
        candidate.relative_to(root)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise QmdPathError(f"{path} resolves outside the workspace root {root}.") from exc

    config.qmd_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return qmd.qmd_add_collection(root, config.qmd_dir, candidate, name=name, pattern=pattern)


def plan_default_collections(config: WorkspaceConfig) -> list[CollectionPlan]:
    """Propose a single collection covering the whole workspace, but only when
    none are registered yet. Empty once any collection exists — there's
    nothing further to reconcile once a collection is registered."""
    if qmd.qmd_list_collections(config.qmd_dir):
        return []
    return [CollectionPlan(name=config.name, path=".", pattern=qmd.DEFAULT_PATTERN)]


def ensure_default_collection(config: WorkspaceConfig) -> QmdCommandResult | None:
    """Register the default whole-workspace collection if none exist yet.
    Returns None if there was nothing to do (a collection already exists)."""
    plans = plan_default_collections(config)
    if not plans:
        return None
    plan = plans[0]
    return add_collection(config, Path(plan.path), name=plan.name, pattern=plan.pattern)

from pathlib import Path

import yaml
from typer.testing import CliRunner

from wakil.cli.main import app

runner = CliRunner()


def _fake_qmd_run(qmd_dir: Path):
    """A stand-in for the real qmd binary: only implements `collection add`
    and `collection remove` against the YAML config file, mirroring the real
    tool's own behavior closely enough to exercise the round trip."""

    class FakeCompleted:
        def __init__(self, returncode=0, stdout="", stderr=""):
            self.returncode = returncode
            self.stdout = stdout
            self.stderr = stderr

    def fake_run(cmd, **kwargs):
        config_path = qmd_dir / "index.yml"
        data = {}
        if config_path.is_file():
            data = yaml.safe_load(config_path.read_text()) or {}
        data.setdefault("collections", {})

        if cmd[:3] == ["qmd", "collection", "add"]:
            path = cmd[3]
            name = None
            pattern = "**/*.md"
            i = 4
            while i < len(cmd):
                if cmd[i] == "--name":
                    name = cmd[i + 1]
                    i += 2
                elif cmd[i] == "--mask":
                    pattern = cmd[i + 1]
                    i += 2
                else:
                    i += 1
            name = name or Path(path).name
            if name in data["collections"]:
                return FakeCompleted(returncode=1, stderr=f"Collection '{name}' already exists.\n")
            data["collections"][name] = {"path": path, "pattern": pattern}
            qmd_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            config_path.write_text(yaml.safe_dump(data))
            return FakeCompleted(stdout=f"Collection '{name}' created successfully\n")

        if cmd[:3] == ["qmd", "collection", "remove"]:
            name = cmd[3]
            if name not in data["collections"]:
                return FakeCompleted(returncode=1, stderr=f"Collection not found: {name}\n")
            del data["collections"][name]
            config_path.write_text(yaml.safe_dump(data))
            return FakeCompleted(stdout=f"Removed collection '{name}'\n")

        return FakeCompleted(returncode=1, stderr="unsupported in test double")

    return fake_run


def _patch_qmd(monkeypatch, qmd_dir: Path):
    monkeypatch.setattr("wakil.integrations.qmd.shutil.which", lambda name: "/usr/bin/qmd")
    monkeypatch.setattr("wakil.integrations.qmd.subprocess.run", _fake_qmd_run(qmd_dir))


def _init(kb_path: Path, monkeypatch, *, skip_qmd_collection: bool):
    """Patch qmd *before* init, since init itself now auto-creates the
    default collection unless --no-qmd-collection is passed."""
    qmd_dir = kb_path / ".wakil" / "qmd"
    _patch_qmd(monkeypatch, qmd_dir)
    args = ["init", str(kb_path)]
    if skip_qmd_collection:
        args.append("--no-qmd-collection")
    result = runner.invoke(app, args)
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    return qmd_dir


def test_init_creates_default_qmd_collection(kb_path: Path, monkeypatch):
    _init(kb_path, monkeypatch, skip_qmd_collection=False)

    result = runner.invoke(app, ["-w", str(kb_path), "qmd", "collection", "list"])
    assert "kb" in result.output.replace("\n", "")


def test_init_no_qmd_collection_flag_skips_creation(kb_path: Path, monkeypatch):
    _init(kb_path, monkeypatch, skip_qmd_collection=True)

    result = runner.invoke(app, ["-w", str(kb_path), "qmd", "collection", "list"])
    assert "No QMD collections registered" in result.output


def test_qmd_collection_add_then_list(kb_path: Path, monkeypatch):
    _init(kb_path, monkeypatch, skip_qmd_collection=True)

    result = runner.invoke(app, ["-w", str(kb_path), "qmd", "collection", "add", "concepts"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output

    result = runner.invoke(app, ["-w", str(kb_path), "qmd", "collection", "list"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0
    assert "concepts" in result.output.replace("\n", "")


def test_qmd_collection_add_rejects_escaping_path(kb_path: Path, monkeypatch):
    _init(kb_path, monkeypatch, skip_qmd_collection=True)

    result = runner.invoke(app, ["-w", str(kb_path), "qmd", "collection", "add", "../outside"])
    assert result.exit_code == 1


def test_qmd_collection_remove(kb_path: Path, monkeypatch):
    _init(kb_path, monkeypatch, skip_qmd_collection=True)

    runner.invoke(app, ["-w", str(kb_path), "qmd", "collection", "add", "concepts"])
    result = runner.invoke(app, ["-w", str(kb_path), "qmd", "collection", "remove", "concepts"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output

    result = runner.invoke(app, ["-w", str(kb_path), "qmd", "collection", "list"])
    assert "No QMD collections registered" in result.output


def test_qmd_sync_proposes_single_collection_when_none_exist(kb_path: Path, monkeypatch):
    _init(kb_path, monkeypatch, skip_qmd_collection=True)

    result = runner.invoke(app, ["-w", str(kb_path), "qmd", "sync"], input="y\n")
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    assert "kb" in result.output.replace("\n", "")

    result = runner.invoke(app, ["-w", str(kb_path), "qmd", "collection", "list"])
    assert "kb" in result.output.replace("\n", "")


def test_qmd_sync_declines_without_confirmation(kb_path: Path, monkeypatch):
    _init(kb_path, monkeypatch, skip_qmd_collection=True)

    result = runner.invoke(app, ["-w", str(kb_path), "qmd", "sync"], input="n\n")
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output

    result = runner.invoke(app, ["-w", str(kb_path), "qmd", "collection", "list"])
    assert "No QMD collections registered" in result.output


def test_qmd_sync_yes_flag_skips_prompt(kb_path: Path, monkeypatch):
    _init(kb_path, monkeypatch, skip_qmd_collection=True)

    result = runner.invoke(app, ["-w", str(kb_path), "qmd", "sync", "--yes"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output

    result = runner.invoke(app, ["-w", str(kb_path), "qmd", "collection", "list"])
    assert "kb" in result.output.replace("\n", "")


def test_qmd_sync_noop_once_default_collection_exists(kb_path: Path, monkeypatch):
    _init(kb_path, monkeypatch, skip_qmd_collection=False)

    result = runner.invoke(app, ["-w", str(kb_path), "qmd", "sync"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    assert "No new collections to propose" in result.output

content.text:
I traced this through `qmd`'s actual source (`@tobilu/qmd` v2.1.0). Short version: the model is downloaded lazily on first use, and embedding is a fully separate, manual step from indexing — nothing auto-triggers it.

**Download trigger**: The embed/generate/rerank models (GGUF files via `node-llama-cpp`) are resolved lazily by `ensureEmbedModel()`/`ensureGenerateModel()`/`ensureRerankModel()`, called only when something actually needs that model:
- `qmd embed` (embed model)
- `qmd vsearch` (embed model, to encode the query)
- `qmd query` (embed model + generate model for query expansion + rerank model, unless a strong BM25 signal short-circuits expansion)
- `qmd pull` — explicitly prefetches all three models without indexing or searching anything

Plain `qmd search` (BM25) never touches these — no download, no GPU init. Models cache at `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/qmd/models/` (`~/.cache/qmd/models/` by default) — this is **not** scoped by the per-workspace `INDEX_PATH`/`QMD_CONFIG_DIR` redirection I set up; model weights stay in one shared, machine-global cache regardless of workspace, which is correct since they're not KB-specific data.

**What triggers embedding, and re-embedding on updates**: Only running `qmd embed` explicitly. `qmd collection add` and `qmd update` (re-scanning collections for file changes) index content into the FTS/documents table but never call the embedding step themselves — they just print "N need embedding, run `qmd embed`" as a reminder. `qmd embed` itself is incremental: embeddings are keyed by content hash (`content_vectors.hash`, deduped across identical content), and it only computes vectors for hashes lacking one — so after adding new notes you re-run `qmd embed` and it skips everything already embedded.

**Implication for what I built**: `wakil qmd sync`/`init` only ever call `search`/`vsearch`/`query`/`collection add`, never `embed` — this was a deliberate scope boundary I called out earlier. So `--mode vsearch`/`--mode query` in `wakil search` will trigger a first-time model download+load on first use, but return nothing useful until you've manually run `qmd embed` at least once yourself; wakil doesn't automate that today.

1	"""QMD collection management: path validation and the default-collection strategy.
2	
3	QMD's BM25 scoring runs over one shared FTS5 index regardless of collection
4	boundaries — collections are a filter applied after scoring, not separate
5	indexes with separate corpus statistics. Splitting the KB into many
6	per-folder/per-type collections therefore buys nothing for ranking quality,
7	and risks double-indexing files that fall under two overlapping directories.
8	The default strategy here is a single collection covering the whole
9	workspace; users who want to filter or exclude a folder can still add/remove
10	collections by hand via `wakil qmd collection add/remove`.
11	"""

33	    config: WorkspaceConfig, path: Path, name: str | None = None, pattern: str | None = None

36	    as a qmd collection. Rejects paths that resolve outside the workspace."""

Same 19 pre-existing unrelated failures, 274 passed. Summary:

**Added `wakil qmd embed`** — a direct passthrough to `qmd embed` (generous 1-hour timeout since the first-ever call downloads the embedding model from Hugging Face).

**Wired automatic refresh into ingest**: both `wakil ingest transcript/text/article` (capture) and `wakil enrich` (Step 2) now call a new `refresh_index()` after successfully writing files — it runs `qmd update` (re-scan for the new file) then `qmd embed` (vector for whatever's new), so vsearch/query stay current with zero manual steps. It's a no-op if qmd is unavailable or no collection is registered, and a failure only warns (yellow, non-fatal) since the ingest itself already succeeded by that point.

def _refresh_qmd_index(config: WorkspaceConfig) -> None:
    """Keep QMD current after writing files: re-scan collections, then embed
    anything new. Best-effort — the ingest itself already succeeded by the
    time this runs, so a refresh failure only warns, never fails the command.
    Not wrapped in a spinner: the embed step streams qmd's own progress bar
    live, which would visually collide with a Rich spinner running at the
    same time."""
    from wakil.app.qmd_service import refresh_index
    from wakil.integrations.qmd import qmd_list_collections

    if not config.qmd_enabled or not qmd_list_collections(config.qmd_dir):
        return
    console.print(
        "[dim]Refreshing QMD index (embedding may take a while on first run "
        "— downloading the embedding model)...[/dim]"
    )
    results = refresh_index(config)
    for result in results:
        if not result.success:
            console.print(f"[yellow]QMD index refresh incomplete:[/yellow] {result.message}")
            return
    console.print("[dim]QMD index refreshed.[/dim]")

def test_qmd_embed_invokes_expected_command(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch):
    captured = {}
    qmd_dir = tmp_path / ".wakil" / "qmd"

    class FakeCompleted:
        returncode = 0
        stdout = "Embedded 4 chunks from 2 documents\n"
        stderr = ""

    def fake_run(cmd, **kwargs):
        captured["cmd"] = cmd
        captured["kwargs"] = kwargs
        return FakeCompleted()

    monkeypatch.setattr(qmd.shutil, "which", lambda _: "/usr/bin/qmd")
    monkeypatch.setattr(qmd.subprocess, "run", fake_run)

    result = qmd.qmd_embed(qmd_dir, tmp_path)
    assert result.success is True
    assert captured["cmd"] == ["qmd", "embed"]
    assert captured["kwargs"]["timeout"] > 300  # generous: first run may download the model
    # Deliberately not captured, so qmd's own progress bar streams live to the
    # terminal instead of being buffered until the process exits.
    assert "capture_output" not in captured["kwargs"]
    assert "stdout" not in captured["kwargs"]
    assert "stderr" not in captured["kwargs"]


def test_qmd_embed_tolerates_uncaptured_output(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch):
    """When output truly isn't captured, subprocess.run returns None for
    stdout/stderr — qmd_embed must not crash extracting a message from that."""

    class FakeCompleted:
        returncode = 0
        stdout = None
        stderr = None

    monkeypatch.setattr(qmd.shutil, "which", lambda _: "/usr/bin/qmd")
    monkeypatch.setattr(qmd.subprocess, "run", lambda cmd, **kwargs: FakeCompleted())

    result = qmd.qmd_embed(tmp_path / ".wakil" / "qmd", tmp_path)
    assert result.success is True
    assert result.message == ""


def test_qmd_embed_returns_failure_when_binary_missing(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(qmd.shutil, "which", lambda _: None)
    result = qmd.qmd_embed(tmp_path / ".wakil" / "qmd")
    assert result.success is False

Clean. Summary of this change:

- `qmd_embed()` in `integrations/qmd.py` no longer captures subprocess output — it lets `qmd embed` inherit the terminal directly, so its own live progress bar (download %, MB/speed/ETA, then embedding progress) streams through in real time instead of being silently buffered until the whole thing finishes.
- Both call sites (`wakil qmd embed` and the automatic post-ingest `_refresh_qmd_index`) now print a plain heads-up message *before* invoking it ("...first run downloads the embedding model from Hugging Face, which can take a few minutes"), and dropped the `console.status()` spinners around the embed step specifically — a Rich spinner and qmd's own live-redrawing progress bar writing to the terminal at the same time would garble each other.
- Verified live: the heads-up message prints, then qmd's real model name / progress bar / completion summary stream through untouched, then wakil's own "Done." confirmation.
- Updated `test_qmd_embed_invokes_expected_command` to assert output capture is deliberately *not* requested, and added a test confirming `qmd_embed` doesn't crash when `subprocess.run` returns `None` for stdout/stderr (the real behavior once nothing is captured).
